the_question: How much could the mask dispute have changed the number the gate acts on?
the_answer: Almost nothing, and that is the case for the statistic rather than a footnote to it.

which_statistic_gates.gated: interquartile spread of subject pixel positions, narrower axis
which_statistic_gates.why_the_dispute_was_about_the_wrong_one: Quartiles are insensitive to a compact cluster at one corner, which is exactly what a fixed annotation is. The extent is defined by the outermost pixel, so a single annotation glyph can set it.

the_plateau_is_necessary_but_not_suffici.what_the_extent_plateau_shows: That the annotation stops pinning the bounding box at 160px of exclusion and the extent reading stops changing.
the_plateau_is_necessary_but_not_suffici.what_it_does_not_show: That the box contains only annotation. The extent stays flat while a wider box removes interior subject pixels that were never on the boundary.
the_plateau_is_necessary_but_not_suffici.what_the_pair_diff_shows_instead: Exactly zero differing pixels through 290px and 360 at 320px rising to thousands by 440px, because two reconstructions of one view differ wherever real geometry sits. The two controls disagree above 290px and the pair diff is right. An earlier version of this sentence said 260px, which understated the certified range by one step of the sweep while the table beside it and widest_certified_overlay_only both read 290.
the_plateau_is_necessary_but_not_suffici.consequence: The pair diff is the load-bearing control. The plateau is corroboration.

a_figure_this_corrects.why_the_old_one_was_too_high: At 440px the box provably contains subject geometry -- the matched pairs differ by thousands of pixels inside it -- so the movement it produced was the spread responding to removed subject content, not to the annotation. Roughly double the true figure.
a_figure_this_corrects.how_it_got_past_me: I took the extent plateau as licence to use the widest box in the sweep, because the extent was flat there. Flat extent means the annotation no longer pins the bounding box; it does not mean the box is empty of subject. The control I needed was the one I already had.

where_the_headline_ratio_sits_among_the_.where_the_headline_figure_sits: The published 26.7x is the second smallest of the nine, not the smallest -- that is 24.5x. Either way it is near the bottom of a 24.5x to 66.2x range, so the conclusion does not depend on a flattering frame.

the_margin_masked_and_unmasked.the_difference_is_the_mask_not_a_disagre: The gate reads the masked frame, so 1.74x is the operative margin and 1.77x is the unmasked view of the same thing.

whether_the_ratios_depend_on_the_axis_co.how_to_quote_a_ratio_about_these_frames: Name the numerator axis and the denominator axis. Naming only one is what let this run for three exchanges: a reviewer pinned the extent to the horizontal axis and varied only the spread axis, while this harness moved both together, so each of us was invariant within our own family and neither family was stated. The operative figure is the one the gate reads, extent_narrower_over_spread_narrower. The others are different quantities, not competing measurements of one.
whether_the_ratios_depend_on_the_axis_co.a_claim_of_mine_that_was_scoped_too_broa: I reported a frame as 'convention-invariant' on the strength of four conventions that all moved extent and spread together. It is invariant within that family and not across the reviewer's, where the numerator is pinned. The label claimed more than the control tested, which is the same shape of error as a report that declares its own parameters.
whether_the_ratios_depend_on_the_axis_co.a_hypothesis_of_mine_that_was_refuted: I suggested their figure came from a row misattribution, because it matched this harness's reading of the adjacent frame to within 0.2. They hashed all nine frames against the ones in this PR and found 9 of 9 byte-identical under the same names, which kills it. The coincidence was real and the inference from it was not.
whether_the_ratios_depend_on_the_axis_co.what_this_does_not_claim: That one pairing is correct and another wrong. Both are well-defined quantities over the same pixels. The gate reads one of them, and that is the only reason this harness privileges it.

the_pairing_matrix_isolates_the_remainin.what_agrees: The reviewer's extent-horizontal over spread-vertical column reproduces here exactly on both frames they tabulated, 24.6x and 18.9x.
the_pairing_matrix_isolates_the_remainin.what_does_not: Their extent-horizontal over spread-horizontal column does not: they read 48.5x and undefined where this harness reads 24.6x and 48.3x.
the_pairing_matrix_isolates_the_remainin.what_follows: Since the numerator is shared between their two columns and the vertical spread agrees, neither the extent term nor the vertical spread can be the difference. It is the horizontal quartile spread alone. On one frame this harness's horizontal spread moves 1.97x what theirs does; on the other theirs does not move at all while this one does.
the_pairing_matrix_isolates_the_remainin.why_this_is_the_useful_form: Three exchanges produced two refuted hypotheses, mine about row attribution and theirs about the axis definition. A pairing matrix narrows it to a single term without either of us guessing, and it is a term either harness can print.

the_floors_fragility_without_proposing_a.stated_plainly: A reconstruction that moved as much again as the worst movement already measured would put the weakest delivered frame within about 18% of the floor.
the_floors_fragility_without_proposing_a.why_this_is_not_an_argument_for_retuning: It is derived from measured movement, not from the nine frames the threshold was chosen on, so it argues for validating the edge against frames outside these nine rather than for moving the floor on them.

what_this_does_not_establish: That the floor's edge is correct. It establishes that the mask question could not have moved the gate, and that the statistic choice was the right one for a reason that is now measured rather than asserted.

provenance.why_the_anchor_is_stated: Two disagreements about these frames were anchoring conventions rather than data.
